Class Splitter

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.text.Splitter
public final class Splitter extends Object
Splits text into parts around a separator: a character, a literal string or a regular expression. 
Splitter.on(',').trimResults().omitEmptyStrings().split(" a, ,b ,, c ")  // [a, b, c]
Splitter.on("::").split("a::b")                                            // [a, b]
Splitter.onPattern("\\s+").split("a  b\tc")                                // [a, b, c]

Unlike String.split(String):

  • A string separator is literal, never a regular expression: on(".") splits on dots.
  • Nothing is dropped unless asked: empty parts are kept, trailing ones included, so on(':') splits "a::b:" into [a, , b, ]. Splitting the empty string gives one empty part.

A splitter is immutable, thread-safe and reusable: trimResults(), omitEmptyStrings() and limit(int) return a new splitter and leave this one unchanged.

    • limit

      public Splitter limit(int limit)
      Returns a splitter like this one that stops after limit parts: the last part holds the rest of the text, separators included. Parts left out by omitEmptyStrings() do not count.

      For example, Splitter.on(',').omitEmptyStrings().limit(3) splits "a,,,b,,,c,d" into [a, b, c,d].

      Parameters:
      limit - the maximum number of parts
      Returns:
      a splitter with the given limit
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if limit is not positive
